newsitem.title: CANADA: Goodale expects Japan investment in Canada to rise.
newsitem.headline: Goodale expects Japan investment in Canada to rise.

text.p: Japanese investors are taking a fresh look at Canadian shares and other investments, Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said on Thursday.

Goodale, speaking on a conference call with journalists from Tokyo where he is on a trade mission, said that Canada's decreasing budget deficit, low inflation and low interest rates were attracting Japanese interest.

"Because of the progress that was reported in the 1996 budget there was a substantial increase in interest on the part of Japanese institutional investors to reignite their activity in the Canadian market," Goodale said.
Japan's net investment in the Canadian economy from April 1 to December 31, 1996, totalled C$5.5 billion, according to the Canadian government.

"Prior to 1996 Japanese institutional investors appeared to lose a bit of interest in the Canadian market, they were putting their investments elsewhere. They weren't looking at enhancing or even maintaining their portfolio," Goodale said.

Goodale declined to specify areas of Japanese investment interest and specifically declined any comment on a question about whether Japanese firms had expressed any interest in Canadian listed grain firm United Grain Growers Ltd.
"I'm not in a position to comment," Goodale said. "That's a matter of private business interests, so I will just let them pursue their private business and I will refrain from offering any comment."

UGG is currently fighting a C$172 million hostile takeover by Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators. UGG president Ted Allen said on March 6 the firm would entertain rival friendly offers but no foreign entities had inquired.
Goodale said his mission was to increase Japan's food purchases from Canada, which amounted to US$2 billion of Japan's total US$50 billion in food imports last year.
Goodale will meet with Japanese food processors Friday. Canola is Canada's single largest export to Japan but pork exports have also risen sharply in recent years.
